accuracy.evidence: Every equation was recomputed from atom counts and checked in a script: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O, 2C₂H₆ + 7O₂ → 4CO₂ + 6H₂O, C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O, 2C₄H₁₀ + 13O₂ → 8CO₂ + 10H₂O, C₅H₁₂ + 8O₂, C₆H₁₄ + 9½O₂, 2C₈H₁₈ + 25O₂ → 16CO₂ + 18H₂O. The general form CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ + (3n+1)/2 O₂ → nCO₂ + (n+1)H₂O and the even-n half rule follow from it. Scope and wording were checked against the AQA GCSE Chemistry specification 4.7.1.3 (complete combustion of hydrocarbons) and the RSC Education balancing guidance. The text says some mark schemes accept a half coefficient, rather than calling halves wrong.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented balancing errors (RSC Education misconceptions; examiner reports on combustion equations): one H₂O per H atom (step 2 prediction '8, one per H', 'Too many: each H₂O has 2 H', p1 and challenge 'hcount'), one CO₂ per molecule (step 1 prediction), counting O atoms but not halving (challenge 'atoms', m9 '16'), rounding 6½ to 7 (step 4 prediction, challenge 'round', p4), doubling only one side (challenge 'partial'), changing subscripts (m4 C₃H₈O₂) and balancing O first (challenge 'ofirst').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagalkcomb is a coefficient workbench for the complete combustion of any alkane: steppers and vertical drags on four coefficients drive a live C, H, O atom ledger with bars, O₂ moves in halves for butane with a 'double all' action, and a chain-length slider from methane to octane self-balances to reveal the 1½ O₂ per carbon rule. flagburn is about flame colour, oxygen supply, CO and soot for methane only; flagalk builds structures. lab_distinct passed under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner changes numbers and the ledger answers: 2 CO₂ shows '2 CO₂ holds 2 C, but the fuel has 3', 3 O₂ for propane shows '3 O₂ gives 6 O atoms. The products hold 10', and a balanced-but-fractional butane says 'Balanced, but 6½ O₂ is not a whole number. Double every number.' The slider step makes the learner find pentane, hexane and octane from O₂ needs before the 1½-per-carbon rule is stated.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions carry tempting wrong options that the lab disproves: '1, because CO₂ has one C' (the C row stays red until 3 CO₂), '8, one per H' for water (8 H₂O puts 16 H on the right and the ledger shows ✗), and 'Round up to 7 O₂' for butane (7 O₂ gives 14 O against 13 and stays unbalanced; only doubling turns every row green).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Twelve distinct wrong-answer messages keyed to the slip: 3 O₂ for ethane (miscount), 7 O₂ for one ethane (single), 8H₂O for propane (hcount), all coefficients 1 (unbal), rounding to 7 (round), doubling one side (partial), heat as the reason (hot), O₂ for flame colour (flame), atom count as O₂ count (atoms), wrong H₂O for pentane (hcount2), O first (ofirst) and H first (hfirst). Six questions rotate.

readability.evidence: Learner paragraphs are short and work one example each (propane in C, H, O order, why O is last and subscripts stay fixed, butane doubling), passing the validator's readability limits. Canvas text is one heading plus numbers and formulas with proper subscripts. The adult text uses the precise terms complete combustion, coefficient, subscript, general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ and state symbol.

no_filler.evidence: No warm-up text; the content gate found no banned phrases and explanation overlap stayed under 12% against every lesson, including Combustion of Fuels (672), Balancing Chemical Equations (50) and Alkanes (121). Each ledger message reports actual atom counts, for example 'Right side: 6 O in CO₂ + 4 O in H₂O = 10. 5 O₂ gives 10. Balanced.'

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 dark and desktop light screenshots of all 6 steps: four coefficient columns fit 358 px with 34 px ▲/▼ targets and 26 px numbers, the gap between columns was widened so +, → and + stay readable, the ledger sits under the formulas without overlap after moving it below the labels, and the × 2 button sits under the ledger. A real touch drag on iPhone 13 pushed CO₂ from 1 to 3 and slid the chain from methane to pentane.

accessibility.evidence: The walkthrough gate completed all 5 tasks with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in light or dark. Every canvas action has a labelled button ('More CO₂', 'Less O₂', 'Double every coefficient', 'One more carbon', 'Check this alkane'), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with each ledger message so the atom counts are announced.
